குறிப்புரை : திருவான்மிகீ ஈசுவரமுடையார் கோயிலைச் சேர்ந்த தேவடியாள் ஆண்டாங்கை மகள் குலோத்துங்கு சோழ மாணிக்கத்தின் மகள் சிவன் பாகங் கொண்டாளான வீரபத்திர நங்கை இக்கோயில் நாயனார்க்குத் திருநுந்தா விளக்கொன்று எரிப்பதற்காக முப்பத்திரண்டு பசுக்களையும் ஓர் எருதையும் தானமாக அளிக்கிறாள். கோயிற் சிவப்பிராமணர் இத்தானத்தைப் பெற்றுக் கொண்டு சந்திரசூரியர் உள்ளவரை ஒரு விளக்கு எரிக்க உடன்பட்டதை இக் கல்வெட்டு தெரிவிக்கிறது. கோயில் தேவடியாரின் மூன்று தலைமுறைகளைச் சேர்ந்த பெண்களின் பெயர்கள் குறிக்கப்பட்டிருப்பது சிறப்பாக உள்ளது. இக்கோயிலுக்குத் தொடர்ந்து தேவடியார் பெண்கள் இருந்து கோயில் வழிபாட்டிற்கு ஏற்றம் அளித்துள்ளனர் என்பதும் இதன்மூலம் அறியமுடிகிறது.

cells.remarks: The residents of Marakkanam in Oyma Nadu, a subdivision of Jayankonda Chola Mandalam, had long enjoyed the land named Tirumalai Sokkan, situated to the east of the Uttama Chola Perattur Pandiyarayan canal, as a permanent devadana (gift to a temple) for the deity Tiruvleeswaramudaiya Nayanar. During the time of Pallavan Kopperunjingan, the boundaries and embankments of this land were destroyed and it became wasteland. The residents of Marakkanam in Oyma Nadu, a subdivision of Jayankonda Chola Mandalam, had long enjoyed the land named Tirumalai Sokkan, situated to the east of the Uttama Chola Perattur Pandiyarayan canal, as a permanent devadana (gift to a temple) for the deity Tiruvleeswaramudaiya Nayanar. During the time of Pallavan Kopperunjingan, the boundaries and embankments of this land were destroyed and it became wasteland. cells.remarks: This inscription reveals that the Pillaiyar installed in the ardhamandapa devakotta of the temple was known by the name Visaiyalaya Vidangar. Due to the incomplete nature of the inscription, the name of the sculptor is not fully known. However, inscription No. 26 refers to the grant of land for the daily offerings (amudupadi) of the Pillaiyar consecrated on the hill by Velur Kilavan Visayalayan Kakkunayakan. Since his name appears as Visayalayan Kakkunayakan and the name of the devakotta Pillaiyar is also "Visaiyalaya Vidangar", it can be inferred that Visayalayan Kakkunayakan installed the Pillaiyar in his own name and provided land for its offerings. However, the image of the Pillaiyar is no longer present in the devakotta.

In the same year Velan Tiruvarangamudaiyan headman of Araisur in Perumanrur nadu gifted one sacred perpetual lamp and thirty cows. In the 45th year of the king, Anba Nayakan donated a Sandhi lamp and twelve sheep. Nulambulan Sottai Alwan alias Sevvurnattu Velan of Nulambur in Sevvurnadu gifted one sandhi lamp and twelve sheep. The Sivabrahmanas of the temple agreed to burn the two sandhi lamps and the three perpetual lamps daily so long the sun and moon endure.

The record belongs to one of them. cells.remarks: This inscription belongs to the reign of Maravarman Vira Pandya. Based on the palaeography, it can be assigned to the 14th century A.D. During this period, two kings ruled under the name Maravarman Vira Pandya. Since no astronomical details are given in the inscription, it is not possible to specify which particular king it belongs to. The inscription records that 25 pon (gold coins) were endowed for the daily service (santhi), festivals, and temple repairs for the Lord (Aludaya Nayanar) on Tirumalai, and all revenues arising therefrom were granted tax-free (iraiyili). This inscription belongs to the reign of Maravarman Vira Pandya. Based on the palaeography, it can be assigned to the 14th century A.D. During this period, two kings ruled under the name Maravarman Vira Pandya. Since no astronomical details are given in the inscription, it is not possible to specify which particular king it belongs to. The inscription records that 25 pon (gold coins) were endowed for the daily service (santhi), festivals, and temple repairs for the Lord (Aludaya Nayanar) on Tirumalai, and all revenues arising therefrom were granted tax-free (iraiyili). This was given towards the Purattadi festival, the santhi of Aramirangkanadu, and temple repairs. Several officials have signed as witnesses to this endowment.
